newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures close higher across board.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures close higher across board.

text.p: Rubber futures closed higher across the board in moderate trade on some late local buying interest in line with higher Japanese prices, brokers said on Friday.

They said prices in Tokyo and Kobe were marked up across the board, reflecting the yen's weaker sentiment against the U.S. dollar and the higher expiry price of the spot October contract. But ample stocks of rubber in Japan continued to dampen sentiment.
"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning but prices rose sharply in the afternoon on the back of higher prices in Tokyo and Kobe," a local broker said.
"But activity was limited by weekend booksquaring and a shortage of dealers and producers in the market due to a trade dinner in Kuala Lumpur,," another broker said.
At around 0945 GMT, February RSS3 rose 1.25 cents to 127.50 U.S. cents a kg.
November RSS1 rose one cent to 177.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25) a kg.
